title: GitLab Patches Critical Flaws Enabling Arbitrary File Read, Credential Theft and Remote Code Execution
content_md: GitLab has released critical security updates for Community Edition and Enterprise Edition, addressing vulnerabilities that could allow unauthenticated arbitrary file reads, credential exposure, and remote code execution. Self-managed administrators should upgrade immediately to GitLab 19.3.2, 19.2.6, or 19.1.8, depending on their supported release branch. The September 10, 2026 patch release fixes 18 security issues across GitLab CE and EE . GitLab.com is already running the patched code, while GitLab Dedicated customers do not need to take action. GitLab Patches Critical Flaws CVE-2026-85706 is a path traversal vulnerability in the repository commits API affecting GitLab CE and EE. Under certain conditions, an unauthenticated remote attacker could read arbitrary files from a vulnerable GitLab server. GitLab attributed the exposure to inadequate path confinement combined with missing authentication enforcement in the affected API path. The vulnerability is especially significant because it requires no credentials, no user interaction, and uses a network-based attack vector. An attacker who exploits the flaw could access sensitive server-side files, including application configuration data , secret material, tokens, or credentials stored in accessible paths. GitLab assigned the issue a CVSS vector of AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N , indicating potential high confidentiality and integrity impact. The flaw affects GitLab versions from 18.7 before 19.1.8, 19.2 before 19.2.6
